source: WP-149 paid read, B1 day 27 (g4.1): every draft reached for «Berlin» before T5 and the day was lost to season_spoiler (docs/implementation/atelier-v2/evidence/wp149-confirmation/README.md). Here the author's page lets Mme Diallo name it; the season's canon guard must refuse the page.

beats: Monday morning after the party: the learner queues for bread at Mme Diallo's.
The queue goes quiet when the learner reaches the counter.
Mme Diallo slips a free croissant into the bag, «pour Odile».
She leans over the counter: she wants to talk.

change.before: The learner doesn't know how the quartier will look at them after the party.
change.after: They know: the bakery is kind and curious, and Mme Diallo has chosen her side.

content.question: And you, how are you holding up after Saturday?
content.task: Mme Diallo veut savoir comment tu vas depuis samedi.

replies.then: Mme Diallo nods and wraps a second croissant
Mme Diallo comes round the counter

content.hook: The notary's office calls: Thursday, ten o'clock.

chapter.question: How does the quartier treat the learner after the party?

content.premise_fr: Lundi matin, à la boulangerie de Mme Diallo. La file d'attente sort jusque sur le trottoir.

panels.visual_direction: Morning, the bakery queue out to the pavement. Steam on the window, trays of bread behind the counter.
panels.narration_fr: Lundi matin. Tout le quartier veut du pain.

panels.visual_direction: Inside: the queue falls silent as Toi reaches the counter. Mme Diallo, flour on her apron, looks up.
panels.narration_fr: La file se tait d'un coup.

panels.visual_direction: Close on Mme Diallo's hands slipping a croissant into the paper bag, unasked.

dialogue.text_fr: Et un croissant. Pour Odile. Elle en prenait toujours un le lundi.

panels.visual_direction: Mme Diallo leans over the counter, lowering her voice; behind, a customer pretends to read the price board.

dialogue.text_fr: On dit que Lila part à Berlin. C'est vrai ?

content.opening_line_fr: Et vous, ça va depuis samedi ?
content.suggested_response_fr: Ça va mieux, merci. Le croissant aide beaucoup.
content.hook_fr: Le notaire appelle : jeudi, dix heures.
content.chapter_question_fr: Comment le quartier regarde-t-il l'héritage d'Odile maintenant ?

content.setup_native: Lundi matin, à la boulangerie. Toute la rue fait la queue.
content.translation_native: Et vous, ça va depuis samedi ?
content.hint_native: Mme Diallo demande comment tu vas après la fête : dis-lui vraiment.
alt_native: Une longue file devant la boulangerie.
La file se tait au comptoir.
Un croissant glissé dans le sac.
Mme Diallo se penche au-dessus du comptoir.
